description: Reference, short-form, signal, and boundary grammars extracted VERBATIM from the deterministic-citations lineage (ALR verifier_core/deterministic_splitter.py == engine legalpdf/deterministic_citations.py, byte-identical block, cited as splitter.py:N == deterministic_citations.py:N) with the toa_maker.py and engine docx_linking.py dialects preserved side by side, never merged. The defs mirror the source rf-composition splitter.py:39-47 (_REF_NUM/_REF_NUMS/_REF_PIN) so each fragment keeps one edit point, exactly as pinpoints.json does for pin_*. Authoring rules: JS-style named groups ((?P<x> translated; groups ADDED by beaver are provenance-marked and wrap existing subexpressions without changing what matches); invisible characters stay \uXXXX escapes, visible non-ASCII stays literal (\u2018/\u2019/\u201c source escapes written as the characters, compiled-identical, noted per entry); Python compiles re.ASCII, JS without u. Vectors: real strings from benchmarks/grammar_vectors/harvested.jsonl (ALR/TOA test corpora) where available; expectations are regex-level (ALR's pure-ref PREFILTER carries extra gates beyond _PURE_REF_RE, e.g. paren-subdivision and bracket-note rejection, so harvested prefilter verdicts are not regex verdicts).

entries.provenance: splitter.py:48-54 == deterministic_citations.py:48-54 (_PURE_REF_RE, tail spliced from _REF_PIN = {{ref_pin}}). The case-name prefix [^,;.]{1,60} attaches ONLY to supra, never ibid, and the pin tail accepts non-'at' keywords (subsection/art/etc) — both discriminate against ref.pure.toa. 'r'/'rules' are NOT ref-pin keywords in either dialect (the Alberta Rules vector). Regex-level note: this pattern matches paren subdivisions like 4(4); ALR's prefilter rejects them downstream, beyond the regex.

toa_maker.py:105-111 (_REFERENCE_RE). Dialect vs ref.pure.splitter: the name prefix (now {1,80}) attaches to supra AND ibid, the signal list drops 'discussed in', e.g. spelled with [,]? (kept verbatim), and the pin tail is 'at'-only with a flat \d[\d\s,–-]* value list (en dash literal in source) — so 'subsection 4(4)' matches only the splitter dialect and 'Oakes, ibid ...' matches only this one.

toa_maker.py:138-141 (_INLINE_REFERENCE_RE). Mid-text reference finder; note spelling (?:note|n\.?|nn\.?) differs from the splitter lineage's (?:note|nn?\.?). Trailing \b rejects 'supranational' (contrast ref.supra-note.linking).

entries.provenance: splitter.py:99-103 == deterministic_citations.py:99-103 (_EDITORIAL_BRACKET_RE). Applied to bracket CONTENT after stripping [ ]: editorial notes route here, short forms (the Hansman vector) do not.

splitter.py:55-58 == deterministic_citations.py:55-58 (_LINK_ATTACHMENT_RE). Matches a whole fragment that ENDS at the connective (optionally after a parenthetical, before an opening <) — glue between a work and its URL, not the URL itself.

splitter.py:80 == deterministic_citations.py:80 (_TRAILING_SHORT_FORM_RE). The capturing group is in the source; the NAME 'short' is a beaver-authored addition. Dialect vs shortform.toa: allows a trailing period, {2,60} length, and accepts a pure-year bracket like [1986].

toa_maker.py:156 (_SHORT_FORM_SUFFIX_RE). The source spells the class [^]] (Python-legal); respelled [^\]] because JS parses [^]] as empty-negated-class + literal ] — compiled patterns identical in Python. Capturing group in source; NAME 'short' beaver-added. Dialect vs shortform.splitter: (?!\d{4}\]) rejects pure-year brackets, no trailing period allowed, {2,70}.

splitter.py:104 == deterministic_citations.py:104 (_SENTENCE_BOUNDARY_RE). Source spells the openers as \u2018/\u201c escapes and the straight quote as \"; written literal here (compiled-identical). Forward-looking: terminal punctuation + whitespace + optional openers + capital. The engine dialect is boundary.sentence.engine in footnote-labels.json (closer-consuming, no capital requirement). No re.I.
